frontier.hypothesis: A real statement duplicated into the switch arms whose copies jump2 re-merges COMPLETELY (zero surviving emitted words) raises loop-time insn_count for free, and enough such duplication reaches insn_count 120 where threshold 119 rejects the four comparison constants at loop.c:1631.
frontier.mechanism: Measured this session: GCC 2.7.2 runs jump1 with cross-jumping off and only jump2 with it on, so arm-tail duplicates survive to loop time and count_loop_regs_set counts them, then jump2 merges them back. The i++ duplication measured +5 loop-time for +2 emitted -- a genuinely sub-1:1 rate that refutes s11's 1:1 kill. The residual +2 came from i++ being only one insn per copy, so the merge also has to absorb each arm's differing branch structure.
frontier.next_probe: Duplicate a LONGER real tail so the merge is unambiguous. Concretely: re-associate the loop so more real work sits after the switch (e.g. compute the next iteration's p at the arm tails, or sink the state-word re-read), then duplicate that multi-insn tail into all five arms and measure the pair (loop-time insn_count from the .loop dump, emitted build_insns). Track the exchange rate per shape; the target is a shape at or near +k loop-time / +0 emitted. Also try `continue` instead of `break` so every arm ends in the identical jump to the do-while test, which is the shape jump2's cross_jump likes best.

frontier.hypothesis: An arming loop that is a second loop of ADDITIONAL real work, laid alongside an undivided 91-insn main loop, exists in this function's semantics or its caller's.
frontier.mechanism: s12 closed every cheap arming geometry: before-the-main-loop is scanned too late (s11, loop.c:435), splitting the main loop halves insn_count below the doubling's break-even of ~60 (s12), and no non-loop construct reaches loop.c:1912 (s12). What survives is a genuine second loop that does not come out of the main loop's own work. The after-main dead loop costs only 2 emitted words (score 5), so a real second loop costing 2 words closes the function.
frontier.next_probe: Read the caller(s) of func_8007526C and the D_800A36A0 record layout for work currently done outside this function that could plausibly belong to it as a trailing loop over the same two entries (e.g. a second field pair swept after the state ramp). Grep asm/funcs for callers first (jal 8007526C), then diff the callers' own loops against this record. If nothing is found, record that as the closing kill for the arming axis.

frontier.hypothesis: The 13-point residual can be lowered without changing loop.c's decision, by changing which hard registers the four hoisted constants receive through something other than case-label order.

What is NOT measured is whether local-alloc's assignment of $8/$9/$10/$11 responds to the declaration order or live ranges of the function's own locals (base / p / i / lim), which set the pseudo numbering that reg_alloc_order tie-breaks on.
frontier.next_probe: Read tmp/grind/func_8007526C/dumps/text1b.greg for the allocation order of regnos 124/126/127/128 and 75, then permute the local declaration order in the candidate (base/p/i/lim -> lim/i/p/base and two other orders) and measure each with sandbox.
